subject: Geopolitics
title: Breaking Enigma
description: A fast breakdown of Breaking Enigma for builders.

hook.text: The Nazis believed their Enigma cipher was unbreakable. Alan Turing built a machine that cracked it every day.

buildup.text: Enigma encrypted German military communications. Breaking it gave the Allies advance knowledge of enemy movements.

discovery.text: Bletchley Park's codebreakers shortened the war by an estimated two years and saved millions of lives.

twist.text: The biggest challenge wasn't breaking the code — it was using the intelligence without revealing the code was broken.

climax.text: Turing's work laid the foundation for modern computing. The machine built to win a war launched the digital age.

punchline.text: One codebreaker changed the war and invented the future.

quiz.question: How did breaking Enigma affect World War II?
options: It shortened the war by an estimated two years
It led directly to the development of nuclear weapons
